steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Britain's geology is remarkably diverse for its size, with rocks ranging from the Archean (Lewisian Gneiss, ~3 billion years) to recent Holocene deposits

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Scottish Highlands contain the oldest rocks: Lewisian Gneiss (Precambrian), overlain by Torridon Sandstone and Moine Schists

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Lake District has Ordovician and Silurian volcanic and sedimentary rocks, deformed during the Caledonian orogeny

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Pennines are a Carboniferous limestone and millstone grit anticline, formed by the Variscan orogeny

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the oldest rocks in Britain and where are they found? | Q: What caused the Caledonian orogeny and what rocks did it produce? | Q: Why is the Jurassic Coast important for geology?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: The Lewisian Gneiss, approximately 3 billion years old, found in northwest Scotland. They are Precambrian metamorphic basement rocks that have been through multiple deformation events. | The collision of the continental plates Laurentia (Scotland), Avalonia (England) and Baltica (Scandinavia) ~490-390 Ma. It produced deformed metamorphic rocks in the Scottish Highlands (Moine Schists) | It exposes a nearly continuous sequence of Mesozoic rocks from the Triassic through the Jurassic to the Cretaceous, with abundant fossils including ammonites, belemnites and marine reptiles. It is a U

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Lewisian Gneiss = oldest British rocks (~3 Ga, NW Scotland) Caledonian orogeny = formed Scottish Highlands and Welsh mountains Carboniferous = limestone (tropical sea) and coal measures (swamp forests) Chalk = Cretaceous coccolith limestone, White Cliffs of Dover
